title: Computer-using agents (CUA)
reading: A single-title slide introducing computer-using agents, illustrated entirely by a 2x2 grid of desktop screenshots showing a recording tool ("DuckTrack") open across several everyday applications on Linux and Windows desktops. No body text is present; the visual carries the point.

visuals.description: Four screenshots arranged in a grid: (top-left) GIMP image editor on a Linux desktop with a small DuckTrack control window offering Stop/Pause Recording, Show Recordings, Play Latest/Custom Recording, Replay Recording, Quit, Natural Scrolling; (top-right) Chrome new-tab page with Google search and shortcut tiles, same DuckTrack panel; (bottom-left) Windows desktop with Microsoft Word open on a document titled 'Please modify my picture as follows:' plus the DuckTrack panel; (bottom-right) LibreOffice Writer on Linux showing 'Top 10 Linux Commands for Newbies' docx, again with DuckTrack.
visuals.assertion: Computer-using agents operate across ordinary GUI applications and operating systems, and human demonstrations of such GUI tasks can be captured by a screen/action recording tool.

concepts.name: Computer-using agent (CUA)
concepts.why_it_matters: Agents that act through a computer's GUI rather than a specialised API.

concepts.name: GUI demonstration recording (DuckTrack)
concepts.why_it_matters: Recording user actions supplies training/evaluation data for CUAs.
